objective.statement: Restore durable repo-memory mailbox access for Codex without sharing or taking over the hook inbox.
objective.measure: The persisted Home Manager hook is the Codex mailbox reader; instructions prohibit capability-less direct MCP sweeps.

need.statement: The attached Codex MCP tool surface loses the signed inbox capability between calls. Reusing any server-side direct-reader session without it is correctly refused.
stakeholders: Codex turns that need coordination context
need.baseline: An unsuffixed session and a prior role-qualified direct session were refused as foreign. A fresh role-qualified direct session bootstrapped once, then its capability-less reuse was refused. The managed hook has a tested persisted-capability path.
need.consequence_of_no_action: Instructions direct Codex to issue a non-durable mailbox operation that fails after bootstrap and risks confusing a safe authorization refusal for a server defect.
assumptions: The managed Codex hook is installed and invoked at SessionStart and UserPromptSubmit.
alternatives_considered: Claim or delete the foreign inbox
Reuse the hook inbox from direct MCP calls
Create a fresh direct-reader session every turn
Use the existing persisted Home Manager hook reader

admission.reason: Operator identified the reproducible mailbox failure and directed its repair.

purpose: Restore durable Codex mailbox access without weakening foreign-inbox ownership protection.
consumer: Codex turns receiving coordination context through the installed Home Manager hook.
contract: The Home Manager hook is the Codex mailbox reader and persists its principal-hook capability. Instructions prohibit a capability-less attached coordination_sweep call. An adapter that owns a separate persisted capability may use a role- and thread-scoped session without sharing the hook inbox.
failure_boundary: No client may disclose, fabricate, or reuse another reader's inbox_uri; change server ownership; or share an acknowledgement watermark with the hook.

evidence.description: A source-contract test fails while Codex instructions require a capability-less direct sweep and passes after the persistent hook reader and direct-call boundary are explicit.
Live direct sweeps establish that a signed capability is required for reuse; hook regression tests prove capability persistence and isolated hook sessions.

falsifier.claim: Codex uses a durable hook mailbox without interfering with other readers.

executable_check.description: The test fails if the instruction requires a capability-less direct sweep, omits the persistent hook reader, or permits claiming a foreign inbox.

non_goals: Recovering, deleting, or claiming the foreign unsuffixed inbox
invariants: The server remains the owner of inbox authorization
the hook persists only its own signed capability
hook and adapter readers have separate sessions and watermarks
a direct reader never retries an ownership refusal without its own persisted capability

assumptions.statement: The managed Codex hook uses an isolated principal-hook session and persists its returned signed capability for subsequent calls.
assumptions.falsifier: The hook regression reports a missing capability, reused hook session, or failed capability persistence.

assumptions.statement: The activated Codex hook delivers its mailbox context to the interactive client at its configured lifecycle events.
assumptions.falsifier: After Home Manager activation, a Codex SessionStart or UserPromptSubmit fails to run the managed sweep hook or does not provide its context.

plane_constraints: Home Manager owns the Codex instruction projection; repo-memory owns inbox authorization.
